transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-15 16:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Shah (Redwood AE), Elena Garcia (Redwood SE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (BlueCrest CISO), Alicia Ruiz (Head of ML), Derek Young (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Procurement)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we, uh, have most people — thanks Mark for making time. Quick agenda: security posture, compliance artifacts, SSO, encryption/KMS and then we can talk deployment options and next steps.
[00:18] Mark: Thanks Samir. Quick context — BlueCrest is starting to move more ML inference into prod, we're evaluating a couple of providers. Top priority for us is compliance: SOC2, ISO, customer data residency and strong RBAC. Also, low tolerance for PII leakage, so we need KMS integration and audit trail.
[00:35] Samir: Totally. So to start, high level, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, we can share the reports. For customers who need isolated infrastructure we offer Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (customer VPC or on-prem).
[00:50] Alicia: When you say "private", is that full air-gap on prem or VPC peering? Because some workloads must not traverse public internet.
[00:58] Elena: Good question. We do both. Private options include a customer-managed VPC with private link, or an on-prem installer for fully air-gapped deployments. There are differences in ops model and where audit logs live.
[01:12] Derek: For our procurement/compliance, we need to see how logs are exported. Specifically we need tamper-evident audit logs, retention configurable to 7 years for some customers, and the ability to stream logs to our SIEM.
[01:26] Maya: We support exporting audit logs to customer syslog/S3 or streaming via Kinesis/Events. For hosted, logs go to Redwood-managed storage by default but we can configure log forwarding to your SIEM for enterprise plans. For private/on-prem, logs stay in your environment.
[01:42] Mark: Is the hosted option acceptable to pass SOC2 audits? Like, will you provide the artifacts showing controls?
[01:49] Samir: Yes — we provide SOC2 Type II report, controls mapping, and we're happy to do a security review. The only caveat is that with hosted, customers often want encryption keys in their KMS. We support BYOK via customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS in some enterprise tiers.
[02:05] Alicia: Can you clarify KMS integration? We run HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS. How does Redwood integrate?
[02:12] Elena: We integrate with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys for dedicated/private. For Vault, we usually need an integration plan — some customers use Vault to wrap a KMS key, or we use a short-lived key exchange. We can follow up with an integration pattern doc.
[02:27] Priya: From procurement perspective we need SSO — can you do SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning and role-based access?
[02:35] Samir: Yes — SSO via SAML 2.0 is supported, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC at the token/role level. We'll share metadata XML and a step-by-step setup.
[02:46] Derek: How fine-grained is RBAC? We want least-privilege so that ML engineers can deploy models but can't modify billing or view audit exports.
[02:55] Maya: RBAC is role-based and supports custom roles on Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have a built-in set of roles (admin, engineer, viewer) and you can request custom roles for enterprise. Token-level permissions map to APIs and console actions.
[03:10] Mark: Talk to me about data retention and deletion. We have strict rules: customer data used for inference must be deletable within 24 hours on request and we need proof of deletion.
[03:20] Elena: For Hosted we have configurable retention windows; we provide deletion APIs and can produce deletion confirmations. For sensitive tenants we recommend Dedicated or Private so data never hits multi-tenant storage. We can also set up a contractual deletion SLO.
[03:34] Alicia: Does Redwood ever use customer data for model training? We must ensure no training on our customer data.
[03:40] Samir: We do not use customer data for training in hosted inference by default — and we'll include that clause in security docs. It's in our data handling policy; enterprise customers can get contractual language.
[03:50] Mark: A couple of nitty-gritty — key rotation, HSM support, and audit timeline for key access.
[03:58] Maya: We support HSM-backed KMS via cloud providers. Key rotation policies can be customer-driven; Redwood will accept rotated keys and maintain envelope keys. Access to keys is logged; we can provide key access logs as part of audits.
[04:15] Derek: Latency and performance again — we need to balance cost vs latency. If we go Dedicated, can we pin model versions and guarantee latency SLOs?
[04:25] Elena: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and low latency. We can set uptime and tail-latency SLOs in contracts for reserved capacity. For Hosted we provide performance profiles but not hard latency SLAs.
[04:36] Mark: For the SAML integration, do you support multiple IdPs per org? We have separate corporate and vendor IdP for contractors.
[04:44] Samir: Yes, multiple IdPs supported for enterprise. SCIM provisioning can handle groups and mapping. We'll send an example of mapping groups to Redwood roles.
[04:53] Priya: Would you share the standard security questionnaire? We use a 3rd-party vendor that sends a 200+ question RFP.
[05:00] Samir: Absolutely — we'll return the completed vendor questionnaire (or provide access to our infosec portal) as part of the package.
[05:06] Mark: One more — audit logs must be tamper-evident; can you sign logs or provide checksum?
[05:13] Maya: We produce append-only logs with sequence numbers and can produce signed exports for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can provide signed exports on request for enterprise deals.
[05:24] Alicia: Any mention of KV caching or user session caches in logs? We want to ensure no sensitive token leaks in logs.
[05:31] Elena: We strip secrets and PII out of logs by default; KV cache contents are not persisted to logs. We also support masking in logs and redaction rules.
[05:44] Derek: Would a proof-of-concept on Dedicated be possible? We want to run a small workload (2k qps peak) for two weeks to validate costs and latency.
[05:54] Samir: Yes — we typically do a pilot on Dedicated with a week-long smoke test and then a longer benchmark. We'll propose a test plan.
[06:02] Mark: About contract terms — we need liability limits, data residency clauses and breach notification timelines.
[06:10] Samir: We'll loop legal in. Standard is 72 hours for incident notification; we can negotiate residency clauses for EU/US regions and data handling.
[06:20] Priya: Procurement will need pricing and seat/licensing model for Dedicated and Private.
[06:25] Samir: We'll send a pricing skus doc, but high-level: hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and Private is enterprise licensing.
[06:34] Mark: OK, quick recap?
[06:36] Samir: Recap: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs, SSO/SAML and SCIM setup guide + sample metadata, proposed Dedicated benchmark plan, and log/export options. BlueCrest to share network/VPN details and internal compliance contacts. We'll schedule follow-up workshop week of 4/20.
[06:55] Priya: Sounds good.
[07:00] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "Redwood Infernce" instead of Redwood Inference, "K V cash" for KV cache), filler words retained.
